name: Refugee & International Protection (incl. Temporary Protection for Syrians)

selection_odds.basis: Turkey hosts approximately 2.35 million Syrians under Temporary Protection status — one of the world's largest refugee populations. Temporary Protection is a distinct status from International Protection and does not itself lead to long-term residence or citizenship.

requirements.blocker_text: This applies specifically to Syrian nationals (and some stateless Palestinians from Syria) under the Temporary Protection Regulation — a distinct status from standard International Protection under Law No. 6458, and does NOT itself lead to long-term residence or citizenship.

This requires being in Turkey and covers three statuses under Law No. 6458: refugee (persecution grounds, subject to Turkey's geographical limitation to the 1951 Convention covering European-origin applicants only), conditional refugee (non-European origin, typically resettled to a third country), and subsidiary protection (real risk of serious harm).

evidence_required.document: Evidence supporting the persecution or serious-harm claim
Registration with the Presidency of Migration Management

outcome.duration_length: varies by status — Temporary Protection is renewed on a rolling basis without a fixed end date; International Protection statuses are similarly indefinite pending resolution

sources.title: Temporary Protection - Presidency of Migration Management
International Protection - Presidency of Migration Management (Law No. 6458)

notes: MAJOR STRUCTURAL FEATURE, one of the largest humanitarian populations encoded anywhere in this multi-country dataset: Turkey hosts approximately 2.35 million Syrians under Temporary Protection, a status GENUINELY DISTINCT from International Protection and — critically — one that does NOT itself lead to long-term residence or citizenship, captured via the outcome_override on that specific group. This mirrors the structural exclusion already flagged on tr_long_term_residence, where humanitarian-status holders generally cannot transfer to the long-term residence route. Turkey's geographical limitation to the 1951 Refugee Convention (recognising only European-origin refugees under the full Convention definition) is a genuinely distinctive and consequential legal feature — non-European asylum seekers use the 'conditional refugee' status instead, typically pending resettlement to a third country rather than integration in Turkey itself. pr_after_months/citizenship_after_months left null for the International Protection group since the realistic timeline genuinely depends on case-by-case resolution.
